title: Entropy power functional theory for Brownian many-body dynamics
abstract: We present a formally exact variational scheme for the overdamped Brownian dynamics of pairwise interacting many-body systems in general spatiotemporal nonequilibrium. A joint free power minimization principle determines instantaneously the one-body current and the global interparticle distance flux. The intrinsic free power functional splits into entropic and energetic rates, where the latter are treated explicitly. The adiabatic contribution to the entropy rate is the time derivative of the equilibrium entropy metadensity functional. Genuine nonequilibrium effects originate from a universal entropy superpower functional. Two continuity equations close the dynamical description.
summary: This paper introduces an exact variational theory to describe the non-equilibrium dynamics of interacting many-body systems undergoing Brownian motion. It minimizes a generalized free power functional, which systematically decomposes into entropic and energetic contributions. The resulting coupled equations provide a complete description of how density and pair correlations evolve away from equilibrium.
main_problem: Developing a formally exact variational scheme for the overdamped Brownian dynamics of pairwise interacting many-body systems in general spatiotemporal nonequilibrium.
main_result: The full dynamics are determined by two coupled, formally exact functional equations derived from minimizing an extended joint free power functional with respect to one-body and pair current distributions.
method: The theory uses an extended joint free power minimization principle, splitting the free power functional into entropic and energetic rates, and employing functional differentiation to derive force balance relationships.
model_or_system: The system is a many-body ensemble undergoing overdamped Brownian dynamics with pairwise interactions, governed by the Smoluchowski equation. Key variables include one-body density ($ho$), pair distance histogram ($G$), and their corresponding currents ($J$, $JG$).
key_observables: One-body current density ($J(\mathbf{r}, t)$), global distance current distribution function ($JG(r, t)$), and the universal entropy superpower functional ($\Sigma_{	ext{exc}}$).
important_parameters: Temperature (implied via $k_B T$), interaction potential $\phi(r)$, and the system's non-equilibrium state.
main_assumptions: The method is presented as a formally exact variational scheme, though future work suggests approximations like 'superpower approximations'.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem by defining the dynamics via the Smoluchowski equation and then develops the theory using the joint free power minimization principle. It systematically derives force fields from functional derivatives, leading to two coupled equations of motion that close the dynamical description.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, generalized framework for non-equilibrium statistical mechanics in complex fluids, extending standard DFT/power methods by incorporating explicit entropy superpower terms relevant for far-from-equilibrium dynamics.
